note.question: How should a firm design fixed fees and usage prices when it cannot observe whether customers understand their own future self-control problem?
note.overview: A monopolist offers a menu to screen privately known sophisticated and naive consumer beliefs. The contract program contains explicit participation and incentive-compatibility constraints and characterizes pooling versus separating mechanisms and distorted per-use prices.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In period 0 the firm commits to a menu of fixed fees and per-use prices and consumers choose a contract based on their beliefs. In period 1 consumers privately learn consumption value and decide whether to use the good, with actual preferences distorted relative to the planning stage. Naive consumers value every contract more because they omit the utility loss from future overconsumption. The firm must leave or manage an information rent to deter the naive type from choosing the sophisticated contract.
